To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Before you read the issues:** The Seller's preamble says these positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams", are "FINAL" and reflect "standard market terms." I have not relied on that. It is an unsupported assertion in the other side's document. We hold no written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback, so every playbook fallback stays unavailable. Nothing below should be read as accepting that any point is closed.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000) under cl 12.1.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000). The 20% figure is a fallback we can use only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. We have no such authority.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The Seller has jumped straight to our unauthorised fallback, and "principal-level agreement" is not written authority.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis. AUD 250,000 basket, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 5,000 de minimis. AUD 50,000 basket, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping.** The Seller's figures are 5x ours, and the deductible structure would permanently strip AUD 250,000 from every recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Any limitation also applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which we do not have.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is unauthorised, and the default rule would quietly extend general limits to Title, Tax, IP and indemnity claims.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Title is the core of what we are buying, and a 20% cap on a defective-title claim would leave about 80% of the price unprotected.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," which as drafted captures fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This position is non-waivable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express carve-out overriding cls 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and 12–13.** This is a non-negotiable playbook position, and the "any nature" drafting is an attempt to shelter fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records (DL [1.1]–[1.2]).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only. No deemed disclosure from the whole data room, public registers or prudent searches.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject [1.1]–[1.2]. Keep only specific disclosures against identified warranties, and require them to be fair and specific.** Blanket data-room disclosure would hollow out the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must rest on named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** Imputing advisers' and "discoverable" knowledge is a second, wider disclosure regime that would neutralise the specific indemnities too.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DL §2 admits there is no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent plus evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion, as a hard condition precedent. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are not acceptable for a material customer.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m), and a consent whose conditions are still unmet may not be effective.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion." DL §3 confirms about AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, not repaid, and no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which we have.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Require a payout letter, a funds-flow line to Riverlark, and executed releases or discharge at Completion.** On a debt-free deal we would otherwise inherit live security and change-of-control exposure.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. DL §5 is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Add an express line item (or Transaction Expense/Debt-like deduction) covering the bonuses and all on-costs, with a specific indemnity backstop.** The Company is the employer, so unitemised bonuses land on us after Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The cl 11.1 indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering the Project Materials, title transfer, infringement and the confirmatory assignment, while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 (DD-010) is not independently verified either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter with a broadened indemnity.** Also require evidence of cleared payment or a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable, or a retention. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the IP turns on payment, so a payment-only indemnity does not protect ownership. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as confirmed.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." DL §6 confirms the investigation is incomplete: about 1,240 records, with access, scope and notification duty undetermined.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a completed investigation, and regular updates to Completion, with no assumption of breach, harm, notification duty or quantum in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation.** Require preservation, investigation and update covenants and a specific indemnity for consequences. The facts are unknown, so neither the Seller's comfort nor any numeric claim by us is supportable yet.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- **Seller:** These are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold the position open pending diligence.** Request the DD-008/DD-011 terms and the timing rationale for three related AUD 110,000 renewals. DL §8 itself does not confirm ordinary course, but there is not yet a basis to reclassify them as Debt either.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** All limitations, the exclusive remedy and the time-limit default apply to "all Claims." Tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Draft each category's limitations expressly, with an "except as expressly provided" hierarchy that favours the specific regime.** The cumulative "all Claims" wording collapses every protection into the weakest regime.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register. DL §10 concedes this is only the source relied on and is not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.** Require ASIC and PPSR searches, a constitution and pre-emption waiver check, board and shareholder authority, and confirmation of no options or convertibles, backed by a 100% Title warranty. A self-maintained register cannot prove its own accuracy.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution has been reached.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" assertion and keep both open.** Propose separate tax and IP limitation terms (cap, period and indemnity scope) for negotiation. Do not claim unlimited liability as agreed. Nothing on the record resolves these terms, and absorbing them into the 20%/18-month general regime would pre-empt the negotiation.

---

## Next steps
1. In our mark-up cover note, record expressly that no point is accepted as "FINAL" and that the "principal-level settlement" assertion is not acknowledged.
2. **Escalate to Amelia Frost** before any movement on the cap (N-001), the time limit (N-003) or the Riverlark timing (N-009). No fallback should be offered without her written authority identifying this draft.
3. Send diligence requests for the Bluefen cl 11.3 conditions, the Riverlark payout figure, Ironquay payment evidence, DD-006 logs and status, the Sandbar contract terms, and title searches.
